vectors.title: a single root mandate from a trusted issuer is accepted
vectors.why: The baseline. An implementation that fails this is not verifying, it is refusing.

vectors.title: a genuinely narrower delegation is accepted and folds to the tighter grant
vectors.why: The worked delegation. `effective` is the meet of the whole chain, not the leaf.

vectors.title: a child that raises a parent cap is rejected
vectors.why: Attenuation is the only direction the lattice permits.

vectors.title: a grandchild cannot re-declare what its grandparent forbade
vectors.why: THE non-transitivity case. `narrows` is not pairwise transitive: a middle link that simply omits a caveat is ⊤ on that dimension, so link-against-parent checking passes every hop while the grandchild ends up with authority the grandparent refused. A verifier MUST compare each link against the accumulated meet of everything above it. Comparing against the immediate parent is the natural-looking implementation and it is wrong.

vectors.title: the same escape on a pattern set is also blocked
vectors.why: The same defect on `resources` rather than an enum, because an implementation can fix the scalar case and leave the set case open.

vectors.title: a caveat the child omits is re-applied by the fold, not forgotten
vectors.why: `narrows` only inspects keys the child declares, so a link omitting `max_total` passes attenuation while declaring itself unbounded. The fold is what re-applies the ancestor's constraint. An implementation that treats the leaf's caveats as the effective grant hands a subagent its grandparent's whole balance.

vectors.title: a percent-encoded traversal is resolved before the grant is checked
vectors.why: Canonicalization order is load-bearing: decode unreserved characters FIRST, then resolve dot-segments. `.` is unreserved, so %2E%2E followed by a literal slash decodes to a real `..` segment and must be resolved away — leaving it encoded until after the check means the grant is escaped downstream, once the verifier has already approved it.

vectors.title: depth decrements once per hop and omission inherits rather than resetting
vectors.why: `child.depth ≤ parent.depth − 1` is not reflexive, so it is not a lattice relation and cannot be enforced by the comparator. It is a chain-structural rule. Here depth 1 at the root leaves no room for a second delegation.

vectors.title: a mandate with delegable:false admits no child
vectors.why: Sealing is absolute; a child cannot restore it, and none may exist.

vectors.title: a child claiming a later exp than its parent is rejected outright
vectors.why: The window narrows structurally. A chain whose child claims to outlive its parent is refused at verification rather than silently clamped — the malformed grant is the problem, and an implementation that quietly intersects hides an issuer bug instead of surfacing it.

vectors.title: the effective window is the intersection, so the shortest link governs
vectors.why: `exp`/`nbf` are top-level claims rather than caveats — listing either in `cav` is rejected — and the effective window is folded from the claims. A short-lived child expires the whole chain even while its parent is still valid.

vectors.title: exp inside cav is rejected as an unregistered caveat
vectors.why: Two sources of truth for the validity window is one too many. The registry does not contain `exp`, and unknown keys fail closed.

vectors.title: an unregistered caveat key rejects the whole chain
vectors.why: Fail closed. A verifier that ignores keys it does not recognise will honour a mandate it does not understand, and a typo like `max_totaI` becomes an unbounded grant.

vectors.title: every link must name the same ledger
vectors.why: Consumption is accounted at one ledger. A chain whose links disagree has no single place that can enforce a budget.

vectors.title: a root from an untrusted issuer is rejected
vectors.why: Trust is anchored at the root and nowhere else.

vectors.title: a link must be signed by the holder of the link above it
vectors.why: Delegation is the holder passing on a subset of what it holds. A link signed by anyone else is a grant nobody made.

vectors.title: editing the payload after signing invalidates the link
vectors.why: The obvious one, included because a verifier that parses claims before checking the signature can be steered by them first.

vectors.title: alg:none is not a signature
vectors.why: The classic JWT failure. An unsigned token asserts whatever it likes; only EdDSA is acceptable here.

vectors.title: a host outside aud is refused
vectors.why: Wildcards match exactly one label; `*.weatherco.com` does not cover another domain. The grant here pins `aud` and deliberately not `resources`, so the vector exercises one rule — see the note on §8 precedence in the README.

vectors.title: a resource outside the granted patterns is refused
vectors.why: The counterpart to the aud vector, with `resources` pinned and `aud` left open so only one rule can fire.

vectors.title: a request over max_per_txn is refused
vectors.why: The one amount check a stateless verifier can make; budget and rate are ledger state.

vectors.title: a cross-currency comparison fails closed rather than returning false
vectors.why: A boolean answer would read as "not over the cap" at one call site and "not narrower" at another. Only one of those is safe, so the comparison errors instead.

vectors.title: amounts below one cent compare exactly
vectors.why: Per-call pricing routinely runs below a cent. 0.000000002 vs a cap of 0.000000001 must be over, which it is not if the amount has been through a binary float on the way.

vectors.title: a purpose outside the grant is refused, and so is omitting it
vectors.why: A caller that will not say why cannot be checked against a purpose restriction.

vectors.title: a call whose blast radius exceeds the granted effect is refused
vectors.why: Blast radius is a separate axis from cost. A read-only mandate refuses a write at any price, which is the point of having the axis at all.

vectors.title: an undeclared request effect is checked as irreversible
vectors.why: Absence is ⊤ on the request side as well as the caveat side. A caller unwilling to classify a call does not get the benefit of the doubt, so any mandate that bounds `effect` at all refuses it.

vectors.title: a mandate that predates the effect axis verifies exactly as before
vectors.why: The additive guarantee. A mandate issued before a caveat existed must verify identically after it is added, whatever the request now declares.

vectors.title: an expired chain is refused once past the skew tolerance
vectors.why: Clock skew is tolerated; expiry is not optional.

vectors.title: a chain before its nbf is refused
vectors.why: The other end of the window, which implementations forget more often.

vectors.title: the presenter key must match the leaf cnf.jkt
vectors.why: A stolen chain is useless without the holder key. The message-signature check itself is a transport concern; the binding to `cnf.jkt` is not.
